name: Kelvar Ube-Mango Cream Soda
description: A mainstream cream soda from Univen's mid-market portfolio, blending synth-ube and synth-mango into a sweet, dessert-adjacent drink sold in wide-mouth cans with a vivid purple-gold label.
flavor_profile: Rich, sweet ube-vanilla foundation with a bright mango topnote and a creamy carbonated finish
cultural_context: Kelvar is a reliable, unobjectionable product — the kind of drink stocked at workplace cafeterias and school dispensaries. It's comforting without being interesting, which makes it a background fixture of everyday Tier 2-3 life.
story_hooks: Univen is planning to discontinue Kelvar to consolidate its soda portfolio, and a Tier 2 community organizer is mounting an unlikely but passionate campaign to save it — partly because the cafeteria contract income matters to the school district.
A Kelvar can has appeared in a crime scene photograph circulating in enforcement channels — the specific production batch narrows the purchase window to 36 hours and three vendors.

A food chemist at Univen has been quietly swapping small percentages of the synth-ube formula with a real ube derivative she synthesizes herself, because she believes the drink could be something more — and she hasn't told anyone.
